title: M/s Maa Vindhyavasini Stone Works v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
coram: Arun Tandon, J.; Ashwani Kumar Mishra, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; bill and recovery relegated to clause 6.5(b).
headnote: A writ is not the proper remedy against electricity bills and a Section 3 recovery notice under the U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1957, where quantification can be challenged under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A prior complaint that does not mention excessive demand does not establish a pending objection. A new-unit benefit claim may be raised in the 6.5(b) challenge.
facts: M/s Maa Vindhyavasini Stone Works challenged bills dated 3 October 2014 for Rs. 24,12,707 and a like demand notice under Section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1957, issued by Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. Counsel relied on a 10 July 2014 complaint as an objection to an excessive demand despite no consumption. The Court found that complaint did not mention any excessive demand. The petitioner also claimed benefit as a new unit.

holding_units.holding: Correctness of electricity bills and a recovery certificate under Section 3 of the U.P. Government Electrical Undertaking (Recovery of Dues) Act, 1957, may be challenged under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. A writ petition is not the proper remedy. A new-unit benefit claim and grievance against the bills can be raised in that quantification challenge.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the 3 October 2014 bills, the recovery certificate, and the new-unit benefit claim
not_decided.note: Left for a clause 6.5(b) challenge to quantification.
